key_insight: The paper turns Fourier analysis of parameterized quantum circuits into a concrete gate-placement rule: a target Fourier coefficient becomes reachable only when the circuit arrangement gives both the effective state and observable support on the corresponding invariant frequency plane.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical design criterion for quantum neural networks, helping engineers place local rotations and entanglers to realize desired expressivity for a given interaction graph.
method: Decompose the operator space via the adjoint action of the encoding generator into 2D invariant planes indexed by Fourier frequency.
Express each Fourier coefficient as bilinear projections of the effective state and observable onto the matching frequency plane.
For Pauli encodings and commuting two-qubit entanglers, derive a placement rule for local rotations and entangling layers that makes a target coefficient reachable.
evidence_signal: The design was validated with a single encoding layer using placement ablations, regression tasks from PDEBench and physics-informed Maxwell field modeling, and tests under moderate simulated gate noise and damping.
watch_item: The rule is derived for Pauli readouts and commuting two-qubit entanglers, so its applicability may be limited for more general encoders, measurements, or hardware-native entangling patterns.
paper_title: Fourier-Geometric Circuit Design for Gate and Entanglement Placement in Quantum Neural Networks
